body_markdown:
It’s no secret that the best waxing results come from a consistent waxing schedule. When it comes to keeping your skin smooth, timing matters—and while there's a general rule of thumb for how often you should wax, not every body part should be treated the same.


We're breaking down the ideal waxing frequency by body part, how you can make your wax last, and how to find a waxing schedule that works for you.


## How often should you wax?


Most people should wax every 3–4 weeks for body services and every 2–3 weeks for facial services. The ideal timing depends on how quickly your hair grows, the area you're waxing, and your personal preferences.


Body Area How Often to Wax Why


Legs Every 3-4 weeks Leg hair grows more slowly than facial or pubic hair.


Underarms Every 3 weeks Underarm hair grows more quickly than most body hair.


Brazilian/Pubic Area Every 3-4 weeks Gives hair time to reach 1/4 inch for waxing.


Face (brows, lips, chin) Every 4 weeks Facial hair grows faster than body hair and is more visible.


How does the waxing hair growth cycle affect your schedule? Timeframes come down to your hair-growth cycle. Hair grows in three phases: active growth, transition, and resting. But not every hair follows the same timeline. While some hairs are long enough to be waxed, others are still developing beneath the skin.


Over the next few weeks, those new hairs begin to emerge, which is when you’ll start to notice regrowth. A consistent waxing routine helps you stay ahead of it, and over time you may start to see a more uniform pattern of regrowth that is slower and easier to maintain.


Waiting a few weeks between wax appointments gives more hair time to reach the ideal length for removal. Waiting 3-4 weeks for body hair and 2-3 weeks for facial hair allows hair to grow about ¼ inch, or the length of a grain of rice.


### Finding the right waxing schedule for you


That said, there's no one-size-fits-all waxing schedule. Your EWC Wax Specialist can help you find the sweet spot between appointments. They’ll help you decide waxing frequency by body part, while also taking into account personal factors like hair growth patterns or hormonal considerations.


## How often should you wax legs?


You should


[wax your legs every 3–4 weeks](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/your-4-week-leg-waxing-schedule-for-smooth-results) , although if you’ve been waxing long enough, you may be able to stretch that timeline depending on your hair growth.


Leg hair tends to grow a bit more slowly than the face or pubic area, which makes it easier for some people to go a little longer between appointments. With consistent waxing, you may notice your hair grows back a bit slower over time. Your hair growth may also become finer, making it easier to stretch time between waxes.


### Waxing your legs after laser hair removal


Previously tried


[laser hair removal](https://waxcenter.com/pages/laser-hair-removal) ? You might still benefit from leg waxing, and you’ll be able to go longer between appointments. Laser treatments don't always eliminate every hair, and some guests continue to experience patchy or sparse regrowth. Waxing can help take care of what's left. Frequency will depend on your individual hair regrowth, and your provider can help you create a waxing schedule for it.


## How often should you wax your underarms?


Underarms should generally be waxed every 3 weeks.


Compared to larger areas, like the legs, underarm hair can be quick to make a comeback. And because it's an area that's often on display, you might prefer to book a little sooner— especially during tank-top and bikini season. Tempting as it can be, the real key to making your underarm waxes last as long as possible is to avoid shaving between appointments.


## How often should you get a Brazilian wax?


For the most consistent results, you should get a Brazilian wax every 3–4 weeks.


If you're new to Brazilians, it’s worth noting that it can take a few waxes for your regrowth to become uniform. It’s not uncommon to feel like you have a few stragglers after the first few appointments. This comes back to your hair growing in different stages—but the more consistent you are, the more synced your hair growth cycle becomes. Over time, many guests notice finer, softer regrowth, more comfortable waxing, and longer-lasting results.


Another reason we recommend waiting 3-4 weeks is that


hair should be about ¼ inch long (roughly the length of a grain of rice) for the wax to grip it effectively. That means giving it enough time to grow between appointments, even when you're tempted to book early.


## How often should you wax your face?


Facial waxing is generally recommended every 2–3 weeks.


This is because facial hair tends to grow back a bit faster than body hair, and it can feel like it makes a comeback quickly. Hormonal influences, differences in hair-growth cycles, and the fact that facial hair is more visible can all make more frequent appointments appealing.


Many guests find that a 3-week schedule works well for keeping brows, upper lips, chins, and other facial areas maintained without making multiple trips each month.


Your Wax Specialist can also help coordinate your face and body services so your waxing routine works with your calendar, not against it.


## Why is my hair growing back so fast after waxing?


If you feel like your


[wax isn’t lasting](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/what-to-know-about-how-long-does-waxing-last) , the cause is usually one of four things: improper hair removal technique, a poorly timed waxing schedule, hormonal changes in your body,


or


improper waxing aftercare.


### Improper or DIY Hair Removal


When it comes to waxing, expertise matters. If a technician doesn’t use proper technique, hair may break off rather than being removed at the root, which leads to faster regrowth. At European Wax Center, every Wax Specialist is state-licensed and completes 35 hours of specialized training to master the techniques that make waxing more effective and comfortable


### Your Waxing Schedule


Hair grows in different stages, meaning not every hair is ready to be removed at the same time. Some may still be developing beneath the skin during your appointment, only to emerge days or weeks later. Waxing too soon can also leave shorter hairs behind. Your Wax Specialist can help you create a waxing schedule based on the area being waxed and your personal regrowth patterns.


### **Changes in Your Body**


[Genetics](https://www.medicalnewstoday.com/articles/326764#influencing-factors)[, nutrition](https://www.medicalnewstoday.com/articles/326764#influencing-factors) , certain medications, and


[hormonal fluctuations](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7432488/) can influence how quickly your hair grows. Changes during puberty, pregnancy, or menopause can also affect hair growth patterns, meaning your usual waxing schedule might need a little adjusting. Again, your waxer can help you adjust waxing frequency to suit your current needs.


### Your Waxing Aftercare Habits


What you do between appointments matters, too. Shaving or tweezing can leave you with hairs at different lengths, making it harder to get a uniform wax. Be sure to follow an


[in-between routine](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/the-3-steps-of-your-in-between-wax-routine) , too. Cleanse and moisturize daily to help prevent hair breakage, and exfoliate every few days.


The takeaway? Noticing faster regrowth doesn't always mean you need to wax more often. The right technique, a consistent schedule, and a little care between appointments can make all the difference.


## How can you make waxing results last longer?


The best way to make your waxing results last longer is to stick to a consistent schedule and take care of your skin between appointments.


A few small habits can make a big difference, no matter which


[waxing service](https://waxcenter.com/pages/wax-services) you choose.


-


Keep your next wax on the calendar.


A regular waxing schedule helps you manage regrowth before it becomes more noticeable and gives your Wax Specialist a better opportunity to remove hairs at a similar length. Our


[Wax Pass® packages](https://waxcenter.com/pages/wax-passes) are designed to make consistency easy while helping you save on a wax routine.


-


Step away from the razor.


Shaving between waxes cuts hair at the surface rather than removing it from the root. That can leave you dealing with uneven regrowth when it's time for your next appointment.


-


Exfoliate gently.


Regular exfoliation between appointments helps remove dead skin cells and can help reduce the likelihood of ingrown hairs. Just be sure to give your skin time to recover immediately after waxing.


-


Don't skip moisturizer.


Keeping your skin hydrated supports a healthier skin barrier and helps keep skin feeling soft between appointments.


-


Give your aftercare an upgrade.


The EWC SLOW® collection features


[narcissus bulb extract](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/the-secret-to-slowing-hair-regrowth) , which helps visibly reduce hair thickness between waxes. Think of it as a little extra help keeping that freshly waxed feeling around.


## When should you change your waxing schedule?


You should consider adjusting your waxing schedule when your hair consistently starts growing back sooner or later than usual. Your hair doesn't necessarily follow the same schedule forever. Changes in your body, lifestyle, or even the time of year can influence how frequently you want or need to wax.


For example:


-


Seasonal changes:


Hair growth can vary with the seasons, and some people notice slower growth during colder months. You might also be more comfortable stretching appointments when you're wearing more layers.


-


Hormonal changes:


Pregnancy, menopause, and other hormonal shifts can affect hair growth, sometimes changing how quickly or where hair appears.


-


Medications:


Certain medications, including some used to encourage hair growth, can affect the amount or rate of hair growth.


-


Changes with consistent waxing:


Over time, you may notice finer or sparser regrowth, which could allow you to go a little longer between visits.


The number one rule to follow? If you're noticing a change, talk to your Wax Specialist. Their expertise is the best resource at your disposal, and they can help you decide whether to move your next appointment up, space things out, or stay right where you are.


Your ideal waxing routine should work for your hair, your skin, and your life. And once you find your rhythm, staying smooth becomes one less thing to think about.


**This blog post should not be interpreted as medical advice. If you have questions about any medical condition you should consult with a qualified health care provider.*
